content:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a compact bilateral capability/handshake for GQA <-> MQA kernel selection. Not the full RFC, just the concrete surface we can implement in runtime this sprint.
matt: +1. we hit this in canary yesterday: mismatch caused fallback to slow path.
kevin: Can you outline what 'capability' means here? kernel features, input shapes, and cost hints?
anya: Exactly. Minimal set: supports_grouped_query, supports_multi_query, kv_prefix_compatible, max_seq_with_attention_cache, preferred_batch_shape. Also fallback_priority hint.
sam: Suggest encoding as tiny protobuf or bitflags? Bitflags are fastest to check at runtime.
anya: Bitflags for fast path sounds right. But we also want a small JSON blob for tooling/observability so humans can read it.
raj: How about this hybrid: 16-bit bitmask for runtime, plus optional JSON capabilities for debug. Bits: 0=gq,1=mq,2=kv_prefix,3=prefetch,+ others reserved.
kevin: That works. Need to list semantics for kv_prefix: does it mean compatible with prefix KV format only, or indicates safe to share cached KV across grouped-query invocations?
anya: Define kv_prefix as 'kernel can accept external prefix KV with chunked lengths and will correctly advance internal offsets' — in practice means we can re-use prefix cache across variant kernels.
linda: We should add a cost_estimate field (coarse) so router can prefer low-cost kernels for non-SLO traffic. Could be enum: low/med/high.
matt: Good idea. Keep it advisory only; runtime still enforces SLO.
kevin: One more tricky thing: when grouped-query and multi-query both present, how do we pick kernel? precedence rules?
anya: Proposed precedence: exact match for request pattern -> grouped-match -> multi-match -> fallback generic. Also use cost_estimate to break ties.
sam: Also need to ensure compile-time kernel selection remains deterministic. If two kernels report same flags, we need stable tie-breaker (e.g., creation timestamp or kernel_id).
raj: Tests: unit test for handshake bitmask parsing, integration test simulating mixed gq/mq requests with varying seq lengths, and a perf test validating cost_estimate aligns with measured p99.
anya: Ops concerns: when a kernel rolls out a new capability bit, older routers should gracefully treat unknown bits as 0. Backwards compat rule: unknown bits = off.
kevin: For private deployments, we might want a feature gate to disable experimental bits. Add flag in agent metadata.
linda: Observability: expose capability blob in Console per kernel, and add alert if fallback rate spikes >5% after a rollout.
matt: Do we want a 'soft-compat' mode where kernel can advertise 'likely_compatible' vs 'strict_compatible'? Might help progressive rollouts.
anya: I prefer simple tri-state: 0=not,1=strict,2=best-effort. But keep runtime behavior same: treat 2 as compatible but enable extra checks.
raj: Implementation note: store bitmask + small proto in kernel descriptor saved to registry. Router caches descriptors and invalidates on kernel metadata update.
sam: Risk: cache staleness causing spike. We should emit cache-invalidation event on update and also have TTL fallback.
kevin: Also need to align prefix KV format versioning. Add kv_prefix_version integer in diagnostics blob.
anya: OK action items: 1) matt + kevin draft bitmask enum and proto by EOD Thursday. 2) sam implement registry + TTL invalidation. 3) raj write tests. 4) linda add console fields + alert. 5) I will draft a 1-pager summarizing tie-break rules.
matt: I'll stub the proto and post in #eng-runtime later.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued for canary branch 'kernel-handshake-v1' — status: pending.
anya: Thanks — keep threads here for narrower questions. We'll iterate next week after canary results. :thumbsup:
